Hi Avery,

Hope you’re well — ACME Legal is running through our vendor intake for the hosted API and they asked if Redwood can provide: 1) a one-page, plain-language summary of the DPA that we can share with product stakeholders, and 2) short, customer-facing snippets we can use in our admin console that explain subprocessors and international transfers in simple terms.

A couple of constraints: our InfoSec is particularly focused on whether transfers to non-EU jurisdictions use standard safeguards and where the subprocessor list is surfaced. If you can include a short line about fallback/rollover behavior when a subprocessor is changed (e.g., notification cadence, opt-out options), that would be helpful.

Can you send a draft by EOD Thursday (our time)? We can loop in our outside counsel if helpful.

Adding a short technical note for the summary and console modal:
- Transfers: for hosted API customers we route inference to the nearest region by default. For EU-origin data with export requirements we support the following safeguards: SCCs + TLS in transit + at-rest encryption with customer-managed KMS for Private deployments.
- Fallback/rollover: when a subprocessor change occurs, our system will not migrate customer data to a new subprocessor without an explicit config change — customers keep their queued inference data confined to the region in which it was processed; changes impact future processing only.
- Subprocessor publication: a machine-readable CSV (subprocessors-current-2026-02.csv) is published with every update and an audit trail (timestamp + change author).

I attached the CSV extract and a short JSON snippet we can surface on the console page if you want programmatic access.

If Legal approves the wording below, I’ll add the tooltip/modal strings to the PR and attach the final CSV.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
